Which chemicals are yours?

Wet-chemistry lab · Spin Physics Group · ETH Zürich · inventory of 2026-09-15

Enter your name, then tick every bottle you use or need. Add a note if it helps. Press Send to the lab when you are done. Bottles that nobody claims after the review round are treated as orphaned and go to the ETH chemical waste facility.

Required before you can send your answers.

What do the hazard words mean?
CMR
carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic to reproduction
Toxic
poisonous if swallowed, inhaled or on skin
Corrosive
burns skin and eyes, attacks metals
Oxidiser
can start or feed a fire; keep away from organics
Flammable
ignites easily
Health
organ damage on repeated exposure
Sensitiser
can trigger allergic reactions
Harmful
harmful or irritating
Aquatic
harmful to water life
CAS
Chemical Abstracts Service registry number, a unique ID of a substance

Hazard words come from the label pictograms in the inventory. This is not a safety data sheet; read the current one before handling.

    The list was compiled from 220 photographs of the lab shelves. Some bottles are only identified by what someone wrote on them (marked hand-labelled). Names on labels are hints, not confirmed owners. “Check first” marks bottles that need a look before anyone opens or moves them. Your name and picks are stored in a Google Sheet of the lab manager. Sending again with the same name replaces your earlier answer.
